title: Palindrome, Ignoring Punctuation
statement:
A phrase is a palindrome for this exercise if it reads the same forwards
and backwards once you ignore everything that is not a letter or digit
and ignore letter case.

## Your function

```
bool IsPalindrome(const std::string& text);
```

Return `true` if `text` is such a palindrome. An empty string, or one with
no letters or digits at all, is a palindrome.

## Watch out

- **Skip punctuation and spaces; do not just strip them with a second
  string if you can avoid it.** Two indices -- one walking in from each end,
  each stepping over characters that fail `std::isalnum` -- need no extra
  allocation and handle `"..,"` naturally.
- **`std::isalnum`, `std::tolower` and friends take an `int` that must be
  representable as `unsigned char`** (or `EOF`). Passing a plain `char`
  that is negative -- any byte above 127 on a signed-`char` platform -- is
  undefined behaviour. Cast first: `std::isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(c))`.
- **Compare case-insensitively** -- `'A'` and `'a'` match.

tests.name: a classic phrase with punctuation and mixed case
tests.stdin: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

tests.name: an empty line is a palindrome
only punctuation is a palindrome
tests.description: There are no letters or digits to compare.

tests.name: digits count, and case is ignored
